races.name: Hadley's 'Hello My Wee China' Amateur Jockeys' Handicap

runners_data.name: Woohoo
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner with a win over this exact 5f Good trip recently and a strong sim-going record (5 wins); Jim Goldie's yard is showing modest form over 14 days but this mare is highly exposed at 5f Ayr and carries top weight of 156lbs — the style fit tag reflects that she is mapped in a slightly adjusted role but her natural pace profile suits this shape well.

runners_data.name: Marajito
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's four-year-old was last seen running sixth on Good ground 19 days ago; holds a 5f win on Good but the sim-going strike rate of 8/15 is modest, and as a genuine hold-up horse he will be last or second-last early and needs a pace injection over 5f that this race shape is unlikely to provide.

runners_data.name: Who Wants Me
runners_data.note: Recent form includes a win over 7f Good which suggests he handles the surface well, though that win came over a far longer trip and all five historical runs in the sample are at 7f or beyond — the step back to 5f looks sharp and his natural hold-up style compounds that concern in a race likely to be run at a steady tempo.

runners_data.name: Water Of Leith
runners_data.note: An eight-year-old veteran with course experience, Jim Goldie's second runner here races prominently and is the most likely of the front-tracking pair to pounce on Woohoo; his sim-going record on Good is thin at 2/15 but he has placed at this trip and takes a 6lb pull from Woohoo in the weights from OR 64 versus 70.

runners_data.name: Our Absent Friends
runners_data.note: Tristan Davidson's eight-year-old carries headgear (hood) and has placed third on Good ground over 5f recently; a prominent racer who will sit just behind Woohoo, making her a logical heir if the leader fades, though her overall record shows no wins from Good-going runs and the trainer's 14-day strike rate of 3/12 is modest.

runners_data.name: Never Dark
runners_data.note: A seven-year-old returning after a significant 261-day absence — by far the longest layoff in this field — which is the primary concern before any tactical consideration; he is a genuine hold-up horse whose race-fitness is a legitimate question mark, and while he has course form, asking him to produce a late run first time out after nine months over 5f is a considerable ask.

runners_data.name: Midnight Lir
runners_data.note: Michael Dods' five-year-old wears a tongue-tie and blinkers and has the best sim-going record in the hold-up group at 9/15 with three places; despite that solid surface profile, he is a natural hold-up horse in a race where the pace map pushes him to midfield, and his reliance on a strong gallop over 5f means the race shape will likely not serve his strengths.

races.paceDynamic: Woohoo is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, she will stride out from stall position and dictate at a sustainable gallop on Good ground at Ayr. Water Of Leith and Our Absent Friends are both prominent types and will track closely, creating a compressed front-rank group but without the aggression to seriously pressurise Woohoo's fractions. The hold-up contingent — Marajito, Who Wants Me, Never Dark and Midnight Lir — will have ground to make up from the back half of the field over just five furlongs, leaving them reliant on the leader doing their work for them; on Good ground with an uncontested pace this is a significant ask. This shape heavily favours the prominent-to-front-running profile: a steady-to-moderate tempo suits horses who can travel close to the pace and pick up naturally, rather than those needing a true-run, end-to-end gallop to close into. The field holds more hold-up horses than the map can accommodate at the rear — Never Dark and Midnight Lir are genuine hold-up types pushed into a midfield role on the map, but neither is likely to get the strong pace or the gap they need on this card.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Woohoo Leads Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Woohoo breaks cleanly and is allowed to control tempo without pressure from the prominent pair.
scenarios.body: Woohoo sets a comfortable, energy-conserving gallop and simply extends in the final furlong before hold-up horses can organise their runs; a sustainable pace on Good ground at 5f suits a horse who has won from this position here before. Prominent types who track her closely — Water Of Leith, Our Absent Friends — are best placed to capitalise if she wavers.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Water Of Leith or Our Absent Friends press Woohoo enough to inflate the pace and then get first run.
scenarios.body: A contested early pace stretches the field and the prominent pair, tracking every move, inherit momentum at the two-furlong pole while Woohoo fades; both are experienced 5f operators who know how to quicken off a handy position. Water Of Leith has course experience and Our Absent Friends has placed on Good ground here, making both live threats in this shape.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops
scenarios.trigger: If pace turns genuinely strong and the hold-up types find a clear run to arrive with a late surge.
scenarios.body: Marajito or Who Wants Me would need a strong, honest gallop to close the gap on just 5 furlongs, conditions that are unlikely given an uncontested Woohoo; both have pace in their form but are dependent on a scenario that contradicts the dominant shape. Midnight Lir and Never Dark face the additional discount of racing out of their natural role here, further reducing the probability of this shape delivering.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos At The Break
scenarios.trigger: If there is significant interference or a slow start that bunches the field and negates positional advantages.
scenarios.body: A messy, stop-start race over 5f could scramble the usual front-runner advantage and produce a blanket finish where any of the prominent or midfield types could snatch it; amateur jockeys add a marginal element of positional uncertainty that is worth acknowledging. Even in this scenario, horses with Good-ground form and 5f class — Woohoo, Water Of Leith — retain residual advantages.

watchPoints.text: Woohoo's draw and break — if she misses the kick or drifts wide early, Water Of Leith or Our Absent Friends could steal a march on the pace and the entire race shape inverts.

Never Dark's 261-day absence is the longest layoff in the field; watch how he moves in the preliminaries — a lack of race-fitness at 5f on a turning track could see him detached from the pack and unable to land a blow.

Amateur jockey errors at the start are a genuine risk in this grade — Mr Freddie Robson and Mr Matt Brown are both conditional/amateur riders on horses that need a clean beginning to have any chance from hold-up positions over 5f.

Who Wants Me has run exclusively at 7f and beyond in his last five recorded starts; connections are dropping him sharply in trip and punters should track whether he travels fluently in the first two furlongs or looks outpaced, which would confirm a trip concern.

Both Goldie runners (Woohoo, Water Of Leith) are drawn to race against each other from a prominent position — watch for any stable tactics signal from Miss Kayleigh Williams' handling of Woohoo in the opening furlong.

races.name: Ayrshire Magazine Community EBF Maiden Stakes (GBB Race)
Now Ayrshire Radio Handicap (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Altareq
runners_data.note: Sole front-runner in this field with a solid Good-ground profile (6/7 sim-going, four places); Paul Mulrennan takes over and should face no early pressure, but the STYLE_FIT flag notes he is racing slightly out of his ideal role in this prominent-heavy field, tempering confidence in a winning performance.

runners_data.name: Kokanee
runners_data.note: Clifford Lee riding for Ed Dunlop (1/17 last 14 days, quiet in form) with a recent course win over shorter and a trainer who wins sparingly; steps up to 1m2f having largely been campaigned over a mile, and the extra two furlongs on Good ground is a genuine unknown.

runners_data.name: Qitaal
runners_data.note: A veteran seven-year-old hold-up horse with a strong profile at this trip and on Good ground (8/15 sim-going, three places at 10f); Rowan Scott partners a horse who consistently finds the frame and whose straightforward closing style suits a race where the pace may just be honest enough.

runners_data.name: Mao Shang Wong
runners_data.note: Daniel Tudhope — a significant jockey booking for David O'Meara — rides a horse who won over 10f Good going and has course distance form; suited by prominent racing on a track he knows, though the recent 138lbs burden and a patchy 2024 form string warrants caution.

runners_data.name: Cisco Disco
runners_data.note: An eight-year-old with three recent wins on Soft and Heavy ground, making this Good surface a legitimate query despite the positive form string; prominent style means he will be in the mix early, but the going concern is the key variable and must be monitored.

runners_data.name: Break The Bank
runners_data.note: Headgear-free now but blinkers previously worn; hold-up horse for Tim Easterby whose Good-going record shows no wins or places, and a recent U (unseated) and 16th suggest very mixed form — likely needs a truly run race to be competitive.

runners_data.name: Thyer
runners_data.note: Tongue-tie applied for Maurice Ahern, a small yard (1/5 last 14 days); form string of 0000-6 is deeply unpromising and sim-going record of 2 wins from 14 runs is misleading given recent finishing positions — this one needs a significant turnaround.

runners_data.name: Ouro Preto
runners_data.note: Iain Jardine runner whose authentic running style is hold-up, racing from a true rear position; placed in midfield on the map only because the field's close-country excess forced redistribution — at his best over staying trips (won 12f on Heavy at Kelso), dropping back to this trip on Good ground is a concern, and form figures of 797 raise questions.

runners_data.name: Leonato
runners_data.note: George Boughey's three-year-old (Billy Loughnane, a top apprentice booking) ran well to be placed twice at 10f and 14f, but his genuine inclination is to come from off the pace; forced into a midfield position on this map by the sheer volume of hold-up horses, his light weight and lightly-raced profile are the appeal, with the tongue-tie switch (to a hood, hg:p) also noteworthy.

runners_data.name: Idyllic
runners_data.note: Paula Muir (3lb claimer) rides for Wilf Storey, who has sent out no runners in the past 14 days; a true finisher from the back whose five-run recent form shows nothing better than fifth, and the redistribution to midfield rather than her natural rear position only underscores that this shape is unlikely to suit.

races.paceDynamic: Altareq is the single confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine rivals looking to press for the lead, is likely to bowl along at a sustainable, controlled gallop on Good ground over 1m2f at Ayr. Kokanee, Mao Shang Wong, and Cisco Disco are all prominent-style horses who will jostle for early position behind Altareq, creating a compact but not frantic early order. The moderate, uncontested tempo this shape produces will compress the field and keep the race alive deep into the straight, rewarding horses with tactical speed and the ability to quicken from just off the pace rather than true out-and-out closers. Prominent-to-midfield runners who can sit handy and produce a sustained late effort are best placed; pure hold-up horses face a stiffer task as the pace is unlikely to be strong enough to create the gaps they need. The field contains more genuine hold-up types than the race map can accommodate at the rear — Ouro Preto, Leonato, and Idyllic are all true closers but are shown in midfield positions they are unlikely to naturally occupy, with Altareq, Kokanee, and Cisco Disco the horses most likely to secure their preferred early slots.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Altareq Controls, Prominent Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Altareq sets a steady, uncontested lead and the race is won by a horse tracking close to the pace throughout.
scenarios.body: Altareq dictates a comfortable gallop, and the winner emerges from the small group of prominent racers who conserve energy before unleashing a sustained run from 2f out; the moderate tempo means those carrying low weight and handy throughout are rewarded without needing a sprint-finishing kick.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Front Runner Wins
scenarios.trigger: If the moderate gallop becomes so slow that Altareq simply steals the race from the front without being seriously challenged.
scenarios.body: With no one willing to press early, Altareq builds an unassailable lead and the prominent riders fail to react until it is too late to close the gap in the straight.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Closer Gets Through
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is just brisk enough to string the field out and a genuine hold-up horse threads through beaten rivals in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: A slightly more honest gallop than expected opens a lane for a midfield runner to pick off tiring leaders; however, this scenario is partly reliant on redistributed hold-up types who may not achieve a truly rear position from which to deliver their finish.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Prominent Duel Quickens Pace
scenarios.trigger: If two or more of Kokanee, Cisco Disco, and Mao Shang Wong contest the early pace and create a stronger gallop than expected.
scenarios.body: A more pressured tempo suits true hold-up horses and could see a late finisher emerge from off the pace, though with several of the natural closers mapped out of role the beneficiaries are still likely to be midfield stalkers who avoided the early battle.

watchPoints.text: Mao Shang Wong and Kokanee are both prominent types who may compete with Cisco Disco for the early positions behind Altareq — any crowding or bumping in the first two furlongs could unsettle this race's shape entirely.

Cisco Disco's winning form is exclusively on Soft or Heavy ground; if the Good going rides faster than expected, his prominent placing may not convert into the late finish his form suggests he is capable of.

Altareq's controlled gallop could become dangerously slow — if the pace collapses entirely, prominent jockeys like Daniel Tudhope and Clifford Lee may need to make an early move that commits them earlier than ideal.

Leonato's hood (headgear switch) is worth monitoring in the paddock — a first-time hood can sharpen or unsettle a horse, and Billy Loughnane's ability to settle him early will be critical given he is racing in a position not natural to his style.

Break The Bank has a unseat in recent form and has shown zero Good-going form in the last five runs — David Allan will need to keep him covered up and avoid early trouble if he is to have any chance of finishing into the places.

races.name: Book The Sounds Of Summer Racenight Classified Stakes

runners_data.name: Crystal Aurora
runners_data.note: Hold-up filly for Ivan Furtado whose recent form includes a third over 6f on soft; Andrew Mullen rides and she handles good going, but her tendency to race from the back may be neutralised by the compressed pace shape this race promises — 19 days since last run is unremarkable.|

runners_data.name: Midnight Steppers
runners_data.note: Consistent tail-ender with all four runs at 8-11f showing double-figure finishes on standard ground; a genuine hold-up type forced into midfield by the crowd of closers in this field, and its history of fading late on good ground makes this a tough assignment at OR 26.|

runners_data.name: Park Lane Penny
runners_data.note: Unproven style type for Furtado and Loughnane who has faded in her last three runs without threatening; 17 days since her last run, handles good going but has yet to show a finishing kick that would translate in any pace scenario — a horse whose profile suits no single shape convincingly.|

runners_data.name: Queenies Pal
runners_data.note: Showed brief promise when third over 6f on soft but has struggled on good and standard surfaces, and her best form is over shorter; tailed headgear (tp) suggests concentration issues, and though she's a true hold-up type, the field depth here pushes her further back than ideal for Jake Dickson (7) to make any impression.|

runners_data.name: Golden Valour
runners_data.note: Veteran of 10 years and 135lbs, Golden Valour is a genuine closer who has won on good going but finds his preferred rear-of-field berth crowded out by similar types here; David Allan rides, and the horse has placed form in good ground, though at OR 48 with declining recent finishes the margin for error is slim.|

runners_data.name: Langholm
runners_data.note: Won over this exact trip and going combination last time out, giving him the most relevant course-and-distance form in the race; Michael Dods' ten-year-old wears tp headgear and, crucially, has the profile to settle just off the pace and pick off rivals — his Ayr 1m good ground win is the standout qualifier.|

runners_data.name: Millbuie
runners_data.note: Redistributed to the front as the most likely pace-setter despite being a natural hold-up type for Ewan Whillans; his style_fit score of 0.80 signals he is racing entirely out of character, and with all his recent runs on soft or standard and no win on good in 15 tries, his ability to control this race at the right tempo is genuinely uncertain.|

runners_data.name: Trais Fluors
runners_data.note: Twelve-year-old campaigner for Linda Perratt with no win on good going in 15 applicable runs; Paul Mulrennan takes the ride but the horse's form at 8f on good is modest and, while likely to settle in a handy spot naturally, its declining ability at this age tempers any tactical edge.|

runners_data.name: Abu Royal
runners_data.note: Hold-up type whose recent form has been compiled almost entirely on standard ground at varying distances, with his best efforts over shorter trips than today's mile; natural closer forced into midfield here, and his stamina profile at 8f on good going is unproven given the bulk of his form is at 11f+ on standard.|

runners_data.name: Approaching Dawn
runners_data.note: Jim Goldie's six-year-old has won and placed at 8f on good going, most recently scoring at 8f good just 16 days ago — the freshest winning form in the race; Lauren Young (5) rides, and while his true hold-up style means he is mapped into midfield rather than his natural position, his peak-form profile and course-relevant distance make him a key player regardless of position.|

runners_data.name: Bantz
runners_data.note: Four-year-old for Alan Brown whose win came at 7f on good going, and whose recent efforts on good ground have been respectable without threatening; genuine hold-up type displaced into midfield, carrying 135lbs — the style fit concern here is real, but his 7-15 good-going record shows he handles the conditions.|

runners_data.name: Freak Encounter
runners_data.note: Donald Whillans' four-year-old wears a hood (t) and has struggled badly in recent starts, including an 11th of 11 at 8f on good going; his form on standard and soft ground at longer trips suggests today's combination of distance, surface and going does not suit, and being pushed out of his natural hold-up role compounds an already difficult profile.|

races.paceDynamic: Millbuie is the sole confirmed pace-setter, redistributed to the front having been identified as the most likely horse to take up the running despite being a natural hold-up type — this means the pace is unlikely to be strong or pressured, and a single, largely uncontested gallop is the probable shape over Ayr's flat mile. The rest of the field is heavily populated with hold-up and midfield types, including Golden Valour, Bantz, Abu Royal, Approaching Dawn, Queenies Pal and Freak Encounter, all of whom are genuine closers or prominent racers unable to find their natural position in this configuration. With Millbuie setting a solo, conservative tempo, the race is likely to be slowly run in the early stages before building through the home straight, compressing the field and reducing the advantage of tactical positioning. This race shape strongly favours horses who can travel just off the pace or in the first half of the field and quicken through the final two furlongs — pure hold-up horses firing from the rear face maximum risk in a race where the winning distances may be tight and the gaps small late on. The field holds more hold-up types than the map can accommodate at the rear; Langholm, Trais Fluors and Crystal Aurora are the horses most likely to secure a prominent or tracking position ahead of the redistribution cluster.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Millbuie Dictates, Pace Suits Trackers
scenarios.trigger: If Millbuie sets a steady, uncontested gallop and the field strings out behind with the closer cluster unable to quicken past tracking types.
scenarios.body: Millbuie rolls along at a comfortable clip, with horses like Langholm and Approaching Dawn travelling on the bridle just behind before asserting in the final furlong as the held-up pack find the pace insufficient to generate a decisive late run.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Compressed Finish, Front Runner Holds
scenarios.trigger: If the slow pace results in a bunched finish and Millbuie, never seriously challenged, outstays challengers who meet traffic late.
scenarios.body: The lack of genuine pressure means Millbuie is never asked a serious question until the final furlong, and a horse racing out of its natural role can hold on against rivals who leave themselves too much to do.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Break Through
scenarios.trigger: If a stronger-than-expected pace or a well-timed move from a hold-up horse launches an unexpected finishing burst through the field.
scenarios.body: A redistributed hold-up type like Approaching Dawn or Golden Valour manages to find a clear run from mid-division and picks off the front rank in the final 100 yards as the race quickens sharply.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Front Fades
scenarios.trigger: If Millbuie sets a falsely slow pace that collapses in the final two furlongs, leaving late movers to swamp a tiring leader.
scenarios.body: The tempo is so pedestrian that the field concertinas entering the straight, causing Millbuie to fade sharply as fresher rivals quicken past, with the winner emerging from those who had the freshest legs and clearest passage.

watchPoints.text: Langholm is the only runner with a confirmed win over 1m on good going at Ayr in recent form — watch whether he secures a tracking position behind Millbuie, because if he does, the race shape plays directly into his hands.

Millbuie's pace-setting role is entirely artificial; if he goes too slowly early, the entire field concertinas by the 3f marker and the race becomes a sprint, wiping out any positional advantage and making the result highly unpredictable.

Approaching Dawn has winning form at 8f on good going as recently as five days ago — the short turnaround is worth monitoring, but if Jim Goldie has brought him back in top condition his form profile is the most current in the race.

With eight runners tagged as redistributed or hold-up types mapped into midfield, watch for significant traffic and bunching entering the home straight — horses drawn widest or with the clearest run may gain a material advantage regardless of raw ability.

Golden Valour, Bantz and Abu Royal all carry 135lbs and race from hold-up positions mapped forward of their natural style — monitor whether any of them visibly struggle to settle in the early stages, as a horse fighting for position early will have nothing left for the finish.

races.name: Glasgow Fair Family Raceday 20 July Handicap

runners_data.name: Mr Withington
runners_data.note: True hold-up horse with a poor recent record at 1m2f+ on similar ground (0W0P in 4 comparable runs), and at OR 55 over a trip that hasn't been kind, Rowan Scott will need a strongly-run race that this pace map simply doesn't project.|

runners_data.name: Off Spin
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's four-year-old has solid placed form on Good ground at 1m-1m2f (3 places from 11 similar-going runs), wears a tongue-tie, and David Allan's booking is a positive — capable of making smooth headway from mid-pack if the pace is honest.|

runners_data.name: Glasses Up
runners_data.note: Eleven-year-old who is a genuine hold-up operator at heart but with six rivals of similar style crammed into this field, Sean Kirrane will struggle to find the strongly-run race needed; OR 54 and a 16-day return from an experienced handler in R Mike Smith, but the style-fit penalty is real.|

runners_data.name: Recobella
runners_data.note: Philip Kirby's five-year-old has solid placed form over 1m2f on Good and Soft and finished second last time at this trip — Billy Loughnane is a sharp booking, and although Recobella naturally wants to come from off the pace, the horse's good-ground record (1W2P from 4 runs) makes it a live player if it can sit closer than ideal.|

runners_data.name: Uncle Liam
runners_data.note: Jim Goldie's four-year-old won over 1m2f on Good last time and has proven course-and-distance form; Lauren Young's 5lb claim is attractive, and although naturally inclined to hold up, this horse's last-time-out win demonstrates it can assert positional dominance when required.|

runners_data.name: Shifter
runners_data.note: Wilf Storey's seven-year-old has a 2nd and 4th in its last two starts on Soft and Good ground at 1m-1m1f, but the stable is 0 from 2 in the last 14 days and Paula Muir's 3lb claim only partially compensates for a horse that needs a gallop it won't get today.|

runners_data.name: Zebra Star
runners_data.note: Redistributed to the lead from a hold-up profile, so this is an atypical role for R Mike Smith's six-year-old; Daniel Tudhope is a world-class tactical rider who will exploit the uncontested lead if available, but Zebra Star's own form shows just one place from 10 runs on similar going and the front-runner tag is circumstantial rather than natural.|

runners_data.name: Manbearpig
runners_data.note: Rebecca Menzies' three-year-old has finished 4th or 5th in five consecutive runs and wears a hood; Clifford Lee takes the ride and on Good ground at Ayr there is no strong reason to expect a step forward, though the consistent placed profile at 1m-1m2f means it won't be far away.|

runners_data.name: Romeo's Guardian
runners_data.note: Hugo Palmer's three-year-old carries a ⚠ fade warning and has only raced at 6f in its three career starts, all on Good or Standard — stepping up to 1m2f from a 83-day layoff while wearing a hood is a significant ask, and Andrew Mullen will need to find an entirely new gear from this horse.|

runners_data.name: Sanny Doo
runners_data.note: Jim Goldie's three-year-old ran just yesterday (1-day turnaround) and has a form string of 848867 — consistent mediocrity over shorter trips including 7f and 8f on Soft and Good; Rhys Elliott's 5lb claim is the only notable positive but stepping up to 1m2f on quick turnaround looks demanding.|

races.paceDynamic: Zebra Star is the sole confirmed pace-setter in this 10-runner 1m2f handicap, redistributed to the lead from a hold-up profile, meaning the early gallop is likely to be modest and uncontested rather than pressured or contested. With Good ground at Ayr and no genuine front-runner to push the tempo, the race is expected to be run at a controlled, even pace — the kind that keeps the field bunched and makes for a tactical, positionally-sensitive contest in the straight. Glasses Up, Recobella, Uncle Liam, Shifter, Romeo's Guardian and Sanny Doo are all true hold-up horses who have been redistributed into midfield positions because this field contains more rear-runners than the map can accommodate at the back; the horses most likely to actually secure a forward midfield berth from those groups are Recobella and Uncle Liam, who have the class and recent form to assert position. This race shape — a single honest pace-setter dictating a sustainable gallop — strongly favours horses able to travel prominently or in the forward half of midfield and produce a sustained run from two furlongs out, rather than those requiring a truly strongly-run race to deliver a late challenge from the back.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Zebra Star Dictates Comfortably
scenarios.trigger: If Zebra Star leads at a measured pace and the hold-up brigade fail to get competitive positions early enough to challenge.
scenarios.body: Zebra Star sets a sustainable gallop on Good ground with no rival applying pressure, allowing those tracking in the forward-midfield — particularly Recobella and Uncle Liam — to time their runs ideally; horses who need a strong pace to deliver a late surge from the back are caught cold.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Forward Midfield Surge
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is modest enough that the midfield compresses and three or four horses sweep past Zebra Star in a bunch finish from two out.
scenarios.body: A slowly-run 1m2f on Good ground at Ayr results in a cavalry charge in the straight, with the riders who have sat close enough to the pace — Recobella, Uncle Liam and Off Spin — quickening first.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Lone Front Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Zebra Star, underpressured and out on its own, translates a truly generous lead into an unassailable advantage by the home turn.
scenarios.body: With no rival willing to commit early, Zebra Star steals first run down the straight and the strung-out hold-up horses simply cannot close the deficit in time on good ground; Daniel Tudhope's experience maximises the tactical opportunity.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Land Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace somehow picks up sufficiently to compromise the leaders and genuine hold-up horses get the truly run race they need.
scenarios.body: This is the least likely outcome given this field's predominance of true hold-up types who are all racing out of their preferred role and cannot create the strong pace required to set up a late swoop; only a chaotic early gallop triggered by multiple horses disputing the lead would bring Off Spin or Mr Withington into serious contention.

watchPoints.text: Zebra Star is a hold-up type pressed into the lead role — watch at the start whether Daniel Tudhope actually commits to front-running or allows the field to dictate, as any hesitation collapses the assumed pace map entirely.

Uncle Liam won over 1m2f on Good last time and is the form horse in the field — watch whether Lauren Young can get the four-year-old into a forward-midfield position early, as that placement will be the key battleground with multiple rivals seeking the same ground.

Romeo's Guardian has only ever raced at 6f and is stepping to 1m2f off an 83-day break in hood — watch for any sign of greenness or distress in the early stages that could compromise the field's positioning.
Sanny Doo ran yesterday and is now tackling a 1m2f trip it has not previously attempted — monitor in the paddock and early race for any signs of fatigue or reluctance that could cause interference.

With six or more hold-up horses all seeking room from two furlongs out, watch for significant traffic issues entering the final quarter-mile — a clean passage will separate winners from unlucky losers in what is likely to be a bunched finish.

races.name: Summer Mile Handicap

runners_data.name: Hale End
runners_data.note: Consistent 8-9f performer for Michael Dods with five wins at a mile on Good; Sean Kirrane takes the ride after 22 days off, though this horse's front-running instincts will be frustrated in a field too deep in prominent types for all to get their natural berth.

runners_data.name: Monoceros
runners_data.note: Three-year-old with a win and a third at 7-8f on Good for Iain Jardine, and T14 form of 8/29 suggests the yard is in fair nick; likes to race with the pace but will be squeezed back from his preferred position with so many similar-minded rivals present.

runners_data.name: Bearish

runners_data.name: Dwindling Funds

runners_data.name: Salam Dubawi

runners_data.name: Brigid's Well

runners_data.name: Leadenhall

runners_data.name: Celeborn

runners_data.name: Theoryofeverything

runners_data.name: Walsingham

races.paceDynamic: Theoryofeverything is the one confirmed front-runner in this 11-runner mile handicap at Ayr and, with no other pure lead type to challenge, is set to bowl along at a controlled, sustainable gallop on Good ground. The pace will be honest but not scorching — a single front-runner on a flat track with no pressure behind them typically sets a rhythm that rewards those who can travel efficiently in behind and produce a sustained run from two furlongs out. Brigid's Well, Celeborn, and Walsingham are the likeliest to race genuinely close up in the first pursuit group, while Salam Dubawi, Gweedore, and Leadenhall will operate further back. This field carries more prominent-running horses than the race shape can accommodate at the front: Hale End, Monoceros, Bearish, and Dwindling Funds are all natural front-to-prominent types who will be shuffled back into the midfield pack against their instincts. Celeborn, Brigid's Well, and Walsingham — who have OR ratings, stable form, and genuine staying ability at this trip — are best positioned to benefit from a race run at a measured pace where a clean early position and a one-run finish from two furlongs out will be decisive. The tactical verdict is clear: patient prominent racers with proven ability at a mile on Good ground hold the structural advantage in this shape.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Clean Sweep
scenarios.trigger: If Theoryofeverything dictates an uncontested, measured gallop and the race resolves into a stamina-based stretch drive from 2f out.
scenarios.body: Theoryofeverything sets a sustainable pace that suits horses who can track within three lengths of the leader and produce a clean, one-run effort; Celeborn and Brigid's Well, both OR 87-89 types with solid Good-ground miles, are perfectly placed to pounce off that tempo.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Midfield Surge, Strong Finishers
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is marginally too quick for the lead group and the race opens up for hold-up horses to deliver a sweeping run from the back.
scenarios.body: Salam Dubawi, who won over 9f on Good ground and handles this trip, and Leadenhall, in fine recent form with two wins and a second in its last five at 8f on Good, would be the beneficiaries as the front group ties up.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Front Pair Outstay
scenarios.trigger: If the pack of redistributed prominent types crowd the early sections and force a faster-than-expected gallop that paradoxically plays into Theoryofeverything's lead.
scenarios.body: If the pace quickens in the first half-mile due to jostling among Monoceros, Bearish, Hale End, and Dwindling Funds all seeking position, the race becomes a true test of stamina and Theoryofeverything's front-running composure could prove decisive over those who fail to settle.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Open Finish, All Comers
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is erratic enough to compress the field at the two-furlong marker and produce a blanket finish with multiple horses in contention.
scenarios.body: In a compressed finish scenario, higher-rated Celeborn and the in-form Leadenhall — both proven at the mile on this going — hold the edge in class and acceleration.

watchPoints.text: Celeborn and Brigid's Well are both natural prominent types who should actually hold their position in the first pursuit group — watch whether Billy Loughnane and Jack Nicholls get them off the rail cleanly in the first furlong, as a clear run for either could be decisive given their Good-ground mile credentials.

The cluster of Hale End, Monoceros, Bearish, and Dwindling Funds all seeking prominent positions early could create a scrappy, bunching phase in the opening two furlongs — any horse wide or checked in that scenario may lose vital momentum in a 1m handicap where position is everything.

Theoryofeverything's recent form is modest (0W0P in last seven on Good) and his STYLE_FIT tag reflects that this horse is being leaned on structurally rather than chosen on merit — watch the early gallop to see if Conor Whiteley can find a genuinely comfortable stride or whether he is simply being run off his feet.

Leadenhall's in-form profile (3W4P in last 15 at 8f on Good) and 7lb claimer Jake Dickson make him a notable watch from off the pace — if the prominent group do contest the early lead vigorously, the extra half-furlong of race he saves could prove crucial in the final stages.

Salam Dubawi carries 140lbs as the joint top-weight alongside Gweedore and Walsingham, and Paul Mulrennan will look to get him covered up from his hold-up position — watch whether his post-position allows a clean passage in the straight, as he has the best recent winning distance profile for this trip.

races.paceDynamic: Ramon Di Loria is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 12-runner field and, with no rival likely to seriously contest the lead, he will settle into an uncontested, economical gallop from the front over Ayr's flat seven furlongs on Good turf. Lope Y Linda is the only other genuine prominent type and will likely track just off Ramon Di Loria's shoulder, meaning the tempo will be controlled rather than pressured — a sustainable, single-file procession rather than a burning pace scenario. This race shape strongly favours horses who can sit handy in behind a steady pace and produce a sustained finish, rather than deep closers who need a truly run race to make up ground from the rear. Note that this field contains substantially more hold-up types than the race shape can accommodate — South Road, Monhammer, Summerstorms Dream, Bonito Cavalo, Bring Her Home, Bobbys Pride and others are genuine come-from-behind horses but several will be forced to race closer than their natural position, with Lope Y Linda and Ramon Di Loria the two most likely to actually secure their intended prominent berths; the prominent-to-midfield stalkers are the primary beneficiaries of this controlled shape.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Stalker Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Ramon Di Loria dictates an unchallenged, steady tempo and the race is won by a horse who tracks him from second or third.
scenarios.body: Ramon Di Loria sets a comfortable pace throughout and the winner arrives from just off the shoulder — the classic outcome when a lone front-runner controls a moderate-tempo seven-furlong handicap on Good ground. Lope Y Linda is ideally placed to stalk and pounce, while Penny Mountain and Monhammer, forced forward out of their hold-up roles, could also produce from mid-division.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Lasts Home
scenarios.trigger: If Ramon Di Loria's easy lead is never seriously threatened and the pace is slow enough that he conserves energy to hold on.
scenarios.body: With no genuine pace pressure, Ramon Di Loria could simply ping a lead, conserve throughout and find plenty when asked in the final two furlongs on this flat track. Greg Fairley will be aware of the tactical opportunity and at OR 54 with recent placed form at seven furlongs on Good, the horse is entirely capable of dictating and lasting.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses in the final quarter-mile, creating a true finisher's race where the genuine closers benefit despite their crowded position.
scenarios.body: Should Ramon Di Loria attempt to go too slow early before sprinting, it risks setting up a wall of finishing horses and a true hold-up type getting a split at the right moment. Penny Mountain, Jkr Cobbler and Toy Soldier all carry horses' form of hitting the frame and could benefit if any pace collapse opens a gap, though the redistribution of so many genuine closers into midfield means the winning angle is narrow.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos — No Clean Shape
scenarios.trigger: If early jostling for position disrupts the expected order, with multiple horses disputing the pace and the race becoming messy and tactical.
scenarios.body: With a field carrying many natural hold-up horses forced forward and two prominent types needing to find their place, early crowding could fracture the expected race shape and produce a ragged tempo. In that scenario, a versatile type such as Lope Y Linda with its Good-ground winning form or Monhammer — who has placed repeatedly at this trip and going combination — could capitalise on the confusion.

watchPoints.text: Ramon Di Loria has a clear structural advantage as the lone uncontested leader — watch whether Greg Fairley elects to exploit the absence of pace pressure and simply conserves energy for a long run from the front.

Lope Y Linda is the only runner with the combination of prominent style, winning form on Good ground at seven furlongs and an in-form jockey (David Allan) — watch for her to move smoothly into second early and challenge in the straight.

South Road's recent R (refused/refused to race) is a significant behavioural flag; watch the loading and early stages closely as any reluctance could compromise not only his own race but the positions of horses drawn nearby.

The cluster of hold-up horses all competing for the same finishing ground means the straight could become congested — watch for Penny Mountain and Jkr Cobbler specifically, as the pair with the most consistent placed form among the closers who are most likely to find a gap.

Bonito Cavalo and Bobbys Pride both carry a flag for fading in the finish — watch for either dropping away sharply inside the final furlong as a signal that the pace, though steady, was still too much for horses who need ideal positioning they are unlikely to secure here.
